Slides worth studying include the strategy-at-a-glance metrics slide (slide 12), which pairs each segment with its key figures in one layout, the capital allocation hierarchy (slide 23), which shows a ranked flow of capital priorities as a diagram, and the Capital Release Unit breakdown (slide 22), which splits invested capital by segment and region. The deck uses headline-style titles and mostly keeps one idea per slide.

decks.title: HSBC strategy presentation, 2011
decks.summary: The deck is the Group Strategy Investor Day presentation given by HSBC Group Chief Executive Stuart Gulliver on 11 May 2011. It opens with a title slide, a forward-looking statements disclaimer, and a heritage and business model section that includes a total shareholder return chart. The main body is built around three repeated pillars: a distinctive position aligned with global trade and wealth trends, a clear strategy and execution focus covering capital deployment, cost efficiency and regional plans, and an experienced management team. Regional sections cover North America, Latin America, Europe, Middle East and North Africa, and Asia, each with 2010 profit, cost efficiency, risk weighted asset and return figures. The deck closes with a summary slide, a report card on execution progress, and appendices on basis of preparation and acronyms. Slides worth studying include the trade and capital flow charts on slide 6, the GDP shift on slide 8, the five-filter framework on slide 15, and the report card on slide 29, where dense data is reduced to a three-column scorecard.

decks.title: Shell investor presentation, 2023
decks.summary: The deck opens with the title 'Performance, Discipline, Simplification' and a purpose statement about delivering more value with less emissions, followed by an agenda for the June 2023 Capital Markets Day and introductions of the speakers. It then sets out the energy transition context, showing an evolving global energy mix and where growth lies in hard-to-abate sectors. A central investment case slide is repeated at the start of each business section and again near the close, which gives the talk a clear through-line. Sections follow for shareholder returns and capital allocation, then Integrated Gas and Upstream, then Downstream and Renewables and Energy Solutions, with each segment covered through its growth targets, capital spend and returns hurdles. The deck closes with key takeaways and Q&A, followed by an appendix of targets, price assumptions, project pipeline, definitions and abbreviations. Slides worth studying include the repeated investment case, the cash generation chart at two Brent prices, the capital allocation table by business, and the project pipeline map.

decks.title: SCBX strategy presentation, 2022
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide and a forward-looking statements disclaimer, then sets out SCBX's vision to be the most admired regional financial technology group. Its mission is to make finance simple, accessible and affordable, with an ambition to reach a THB 1 trillion valuation. The middle sections examine three global trends that shape its investments: financial inclusion for underserved segments through digital lenders, the digital asset economy built on blockchain and Web 3.0, and green tech, framed as a USD 50 billion opportunity. The deck then presents a five-theme portfolio structure and a three-phase strategy running over five years. It also covers three Centers of Excellence and two growth accelerators, financial targets for digital lenders, and a Better Bank plan with cost-to-income and ROE goals. Regional expansion steps follow, along with governance and investment discipline. The closing slides list selected awards and summarize why SCBX is positioned to grow. Slides use short headline-style titles and simple diagrams for the three-phase plan and portfolio structure, and many repeat the phase graphic to show progress.

decks.title: Westlife Foodworld strategy presentation, 2022
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide for the Strategy Day held on December 1, 2022, followed by a safe harbour disclosure and a short note on the company's new name. It then sets out the vision and mission, values, and the success enablers that underpin the strategy. A scorecard reviews performance against the earlier Vision 2022 targets on sales, profitability, and network expansion. Five success drivers follow: menu management, omnichannel, network expansion, cost saving, and capital efficiency. The middle sections cover industry trends, the foodservice market structure, and a menu strategy built around burgers, chicken, and coffee. The deck then presents Vision 2027 across four pillars: meals leadership, omnichannel, network expansion, and operating performance. It closes with long-term value creation levers, governance and leadership, ESG initiatives, and a summary of 2027 targets with a thank-you and investor relations contact. Slides worth studying include the Vision 2022 scorecard on slides 6 and 7, the pricing ladder on slide 28, and the market construct on slide 18.

decks.title: IGO Limited strategy presentation, 2024
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide reading 'Discover | Develop | Deliver: IGO's path to 2035', followed by a contents page that lists the sections. It moves through a market context section on the energy transition, EV adoption and battery raw materials, with separate slides on lithium, copper and nickel. A purpose and strategy section follows, covering the company's purpose, its strategy on a page, its 2035 portfolio, strategic themes, objectives over three time horizons and a capital allocation framework. The delivery section covers safety, sustainability, leadership, the TLEA joint venture, Greenbushes, Kwinana, the nickel business, exploration and commercial capability, with financial performance and dividend history after. It closes with a summary slide, a unique value proposition and a cautionary statement, and an appendix holds the board and the partnership, technical and playbook pillars. Several slides are worth studying: the market context slides use a single headline per slide with a chart that carries the argument, and the Greenbushes and Kwinana slides pair operating data with plain takeaways.

decks.title: Salesforce product launch
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide for the New Financial Services Cloud Editions and Winter '27 (264) release, followed by a thank-you slide listing customer groups, a forward-looking statements disclaimer, and an agenda. It moves through a pricing and editions section that compares Core, Advanced and Max tiers and bundles, then covers banking service and origination updates, wealth management features for advisors including the Agentic Advisor, Run My Day and Enhanced Client Details, insurance claims intake and financial authority controls, group benefits capabilities, and a sneak peek at agentic underwriting. The closing sections are a set of upcoming features and a final thank-you slide. Several slides use side-by-side comparisons of value and price, and the wealth section frames its problem with a short sequence of pain points before showing the product. Slides worth studying include the editions value comparison on slide 11, the advisor problem framing on slide 20, the claims intake flow on slide 35, and the group benefits challenge and solution split on slide 40.

decks.title: Signify sales deck
decks.summary: This sales deck for the OptiVision LED gen3.5 floodlight opens with a title slide and a contents page listing five sections: an introduction to the product, a product overview, the Service tag system, dimensional drawings and product specifications. It then moves through the company's sports lighting credentials, a feature breakdown of the luminaire covering flexibility, efficiency, iconic design, future-proofing and ease of installation, and an overview of the Interact smart lighting platform. A dedicated section explains the Signify Service tag app for installation and maintenance, followed by detailed technical tables on luminaire types, light output, weights, materials, electrical connection and certifications. The deck closes with a slide on Signify as a partner and its brand portfolio, and a final page featuring Signify's partnership with a Formula 1 team. Slides worth studying include the product-and-callout layout on slide 5, where feature labels sit around a large product image, and the four-step numbered install sequence on slide 12. The contact sheets show a restrained green and dark grey palette, consistent headline placement, and photography that carries the sports context.

decks.title: Signify sales deck, 2025
decks.summary: The deck is a sales presentation for the CitySoul LED gen2 urban street luminaire family. It opens with a cover and a contents page, then introduces the product family and its design intent, followed by key benefits such as urban integration, comfort, connectivity and maintenance. The middle sections cover the family overview with its two sizes and mounting options, the bracket and pole range, and the application areas for city centre, residential and traffic routes. It then turns to connectivity through the Interact smart lighting platform and the Service tag QR-code maintenance app, with a step-by-step installation and maintenance flow. The LEDgine optics and engine section explains standardised light distributions, followed by a product specifications section with dimensions and technical data. The deck closes with a company and brand overview and a contact page. Slides worth studying include the family overview diagram (slide 5), the bracket comparison photography (slide 7), the application areas layout (slide 9), and the Service tag installation icon sequence (slide 12).

decks.title: Elron Ventures fund presentation, 2026
decks.summary: The deck opens with a legal disclaimer covering forward-looking statements and the unaudited nature of the data, then a corporate overview of Elron Ventures as Israel's first evergreen fund, founded in 1961 and partnered with Rafael for over three decades. It moves into the 2026 strategy, a 2025 year-in-review, a G&A expense reduction chart, a net asset value snapshot, and the management and joint team with Rafael. Next come the defense-tech and deep-tech portfolio, the RDC partnership and new M&A-led strategy, and a market sizing section on defense spending and VC activity. The middle of the deck covers the CyberFuture micro fund and a series of company deep dives, including Raven, OpenLegacy, Tamnoon and CyberRidge, each with a problem, product, market and status arrangement. It closes with a CartiHeal update on the earn-out and a thank-you slide with contacts. Slides worth studying include the portfolio overview grid on slides 30 and 31, the Raven status slide, and the deep-dive template repeated across slides 36, 41 and 46.

decks.title: LinkedIn pitch deck, 2004
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide and the claim that LinkedIn is "Professional People Search 2.0," contrasting networked search with flat directories. It draws parallels to eBay, PayPal and Google, each shown as a 1.0 versus 2.0 comparison. Next comes the problem, the network-first growth strategy, and competitive position against rival professional networks. Three revenue products follow: InLeads (targeted search ads), Opportunities (network-filtered job listings) and Network Plus (a paid subscription extending reach). Each product receives market sizing with comparables and charts of online advertising and job market revenue. The middle section covers pricing, launch timing, the business model and margins, and a five-year financial table projecting operating profitability in 2005. The deck closes with the team, the board and investors, and a short summary slide. Slide 5 is worth studying for its side-by-side 1.0 versus 2.0 layout that makes the network argument at a glance. Slide 33 reduces the financials to a single table with a clear operating margin line. Slides 12 and 13 show market share over time with a simple pie-style chart and a one-line takeaway.

decks.title: Merck & Co., Inc. conference talk, 2026
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide for Merck's presentation at the JP Morgan Healthcare Conference, followed by a Business and Pipeline Update delivered by the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, and a forward-looking statement disclaimer. It then moves through the company's business development activity, its 2025 approvals and trial milestones across oncology, cardiometabolic, infectious disease and animal health, and launch revenue for newer products. Next it sizes the commercial opportunity from new growth drivers against consensus KEYTRUDA sales, and walks through ten key programs and additional pipeline programs. A timeline slide lays out upcoming Phase 3 readouts through 2027. The closing section summarises the strategic priorities, followed by a Q&A slide and an appendix with updated opportunity estimates by therapeutic area and an acronym list. Slides 11, 12 and 19 are worth studying for how large numbers and pipeline categories are presented as simple visual comparisons.

decks.title: Merck & Co. (MSD outside the US and Canada) course deck, 2024
decks.company: Merck & Co. (MSD outside the US and Canada)
decks.summary: This is a healthcare professional education deck from MSD Oncology about KEYNOTE-189, a Phase 3 trial of KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab) plus chemotherapy as first-line treatment for metastatic non-squamous NSCLC. It opens with a regulatory and prescribing title slide, followed by a note on external links and abbreviations, then the clinical rationale, the current guideline position and the licensed UK indications. The middle of the deck covers the trial itself: study design, definitions of analyses, statistical considerations, patient baseline characteristics and PD-L1 subgroups. Efficacy then follows through overall survival, progression-free survival, response rates and duration of response, first at the original analysis and then in the 5-year update. Safety data, including adverse events, immune-mediated events and renal events, come next, followed by post-hoc analyses in patients with liver or brain metastases and quality-of-life results. The deck closes with efficacy and safety summary slides and a health-related quality of life summary. Slides worth studying include the timeline-style indications graphic on slide 6, the study design flow chart on slide 10, and the subgroup forest plots, which are built as clear comparison visuals.

decks.title: GE HealthCare investor presentation, 2022
decks.summary: The deck is the investor day presentation GE HealthCare gave on December 8, 2022, ahead of its spin-off from General Electric. It opens with an agenda and a disclaimer, then a catalyst slide and board and leadership introductions. The vision section frames the company's goal of creating a world where healthcare has no limits, followed by its market size, a four-segment leadership overview and a precision care strategy. Each business is then covered in turn: Imaging, Ultrasound, Patient Care Solutions and Pharmaceutical Diagnostics, with segment-specific markets, pipelines and financials. Commercial strategy and a financial strategy section follow, with a recurring revenue split and a medium-term margin bridge. The deck closes with a value creation summary, a closing slide and supplemental non-GAAP material. Slides worth studying include the medium-term financial targets that repeat as a bookend, the segment-by-segment structure with consistent market-size and growth callouts, and the Lean margin bridge. Many slides use a single headline claim with supporting figures in a clean grid.

decks.title: Revolut pitch deck, 2015
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide naming Revolut and its founder, then moves into a problem statement: sending and spending money abroad is expensive, inconvenient and hidden in fees. It sizes the market with a sequence of figures on cross-currency transaction volume, fees lost to spreads, and travellers and expats, before narrowing to a UK initial target. The solution is shown as three verbs (exchange, send, spend) with a short explanatory video link. The business model section sets out a freemium ladder of Free, Basic and Pro tiers alongside a viral referral mechanic. Marketing, competition, differentiators, traction, team, financial projections and the funding ask follow in order. The closing slide lists use of funds across hiring, growing the freemium base and preparing a Series A. Several slides are worth studying: the business model slide shows how three tiers are compared in a single layout, the competition slide frames rivals through customer use cases rather than feature checklists, and the projections slide lays out a five-year table with a clear summary of revenue, costs and profit.

decks.title: Climeworks keynote, 2023
decks.summary: The deck is the opening keynote from Climeworks' Direct Air Capture Summit 2023, given by its CEO and published as a PDF. It opens with a bold headline slide, "In 15 years", sourced to a BloombergNEF study, which sets the time horizon for the argument. The middle section builds a case in sequence. A survey-based chart shows how carbon removal share in corporate portfolios is expected to grow toward 2030, followed by a breakdown of a carbon portfolio over time to 2050. A statement then notes that direct air capture has clear benefits: no arable land is needed, it is fully additional, and it is fully measurable. An IPCC chart compares the mitigation potential of several removal methods, and a slide covers the capture-to-removal process with its losses and third-party verification. A slide on cost per ton and cost of goods sold, plus a photovoltaic cost curve framed as a "cost mountain" that technology must climb, support the scale-up theme. The closing slides turn to the portfolio mix, suggesting about 40 percent engineered removal by 2030.

decks.title: Cisco Systems conference talk, 2020
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide and an introduction of Rakesh Chopra, a Cisco Fellow, who is speaking at the Ethernet Alliance Technology Exploration Forum. It then surveys system architectures for fixed, centralized, and distributed switches, using simple block diagrams that show retimers, muxes, and optics. The middle sections track switch silicon bandwidth and SerDes speeds over twelve years and break down power consumption by component. A memorable line states that power is the main limit to what can be built and deployed. Later sections argue that co-packaged optics will become necessary as data rates and distances grow, and compare scale-out and scale-up designs using charts of server counts against switch radix and network layers. Further slides project radix and lane options for 800GE and 1.6TE generations and show how each system architecture would adopt 224G signaling. The deck closes with a summary of moral, business, and technology imperatives and a call to action to start 224G development now.

decks.title: NVIDIA keynote, 2026
decks.summary: The deck is the keynote from NVIDIA's GTC 2026 event, presented as a long sequence of slides that mostly carry a single claim each. It opens with a title sequence and then a segment on data, framing structured data as the ground truth of AI and unstructured data as its context, supported by customer quotes and cost or speed figures from enterprise data platforms. The middle section covers the NVIDIA AI platform, showing the ecosystem of cloud, OEM and software partners as tiled logo slides. An inference segment follows, with throughput-versus-interactivity charts comparing hardware generations and linking token cost to company revenue. Later slides introduce the Vera Rubin platform, the Groq 3 LPU and LPX inference system, a roadmap from Blackwell through Feynman, and the DSX AI factory platform for facilities. The closing section turns to agents and open models, covering NemoClaw, the Nemotron model family, and a coalition of regional AI partners.

decks.title: Intel keynote, 2023
decks.summary: This deck is the keynote from Intel Innovation 2023, presented by CEO Pat Gelsinger. It opens with a forward-looking statements disclaimer, then introduces Gelsinger and the theme of bringing AI everywhere, from client and edge to network and cloud. A guest segment with ai.io, a sports science company, shows Intel hardware running a performance application, followed by a QR code for further information. The middle section covers the scale of the silicon industry, framed as a $574B silicon industry powering an $8 trillion global tech economy, and the idea of Siliconomy, with a growth figure for connected devices. It then moves to Intel Developer Cloud, Intel's process and foundry roadmap from Intel 7 through Intel 18A, a list of UCIe ecosystem partners, and a comparison of packaging technology. Later sections cover the Core Ultra and Xeon launches, quantum and neuromorphic research, and the Project Strata software initiative. The closing slides recap the roadmap, introduce a guest speaker, and present a notices page.

decks.title: BASF investor presentation, 2024
decks.summary: The deck is Anup Kothari's segment presentation for the BASF Capital Markets Day in September 2024, covering the Industrial Solutions business. It opens with a title slide, then a cautionary note on forward-looking statements. The core content follows: the segment's role in the BASF portfolio and its 2023 sales of €8.0 billion, a review of 2019 to 2023 earnings and ROCE, and a summary of the portfolio moves and the targeted EBITDA bsi increase. The middle sections are organized around four strategic priorities for 2024 to 2028: growing with leading market positions, accelerating growth in electronic materials, driving cost efficiencies, and leveraging investments for capital efficiency. Each priority is illustrated with market share tables, growth rate estimates, customer examples such as the HyCon construction additives and the EnviNOx catalyst partnership, and a semiconductor footprint map. The deck closes with a summary slide restating the targeted increase of €400 million to €500 million by 2028. Slides 4, 7, 10 and 13 are worth studying for their chart and table construction.

decks.title: Zealand Pharma investor presentation, 2025
decks.summary: The deck opens with a forward-looking statements disclaimer, then a provocative title slide and a framing of obesity as a civilisation-scale health challenge. It moves through the GLP-1 revolution, the company's pipeline and its collaboration with Roche on petrelintide, and a roadmap toward a fully integrated biotech by 2030. Mid-deck sections cover unmet needs in weight management, consumer and prescriber segments, and treatment persistence. Later sections are presented by different speakers: survodutide in obesity and MASH with Phase 2 and Phase 3 data, an explainer on amylin biology and clinical evidence for amylin analogs, and petrelintide's amylin franchise. The closing sections cover the company's pipeline engine and how it funds and scales the business, followed by Q&A. Slides worth studying include the agenda dividers that repeat the running order with the current section highlighted, the dense pipeline table on slide 17, the segmented audience slides on 23 and 24, and the Phase 2 survodutide dose-response chart on slide 42. The deck relies heavily on clinical charts with footnoted sources and uses a consistent section-divider system throughout.

decks.title: J.P. Morgan Asset Management fund presentation, 2025
decks.summary: This 3Q 2025 strategy review for the JPMorgan Equity Income separately managed account is a numbered 38-slide deck. It opens with a cover and table of contents, then a Capabilities section covering the firm's roughly $4T in assets under supervision, its global equities resources, and equity assets under management. An Expertise section introduces the portfolio management and research team with experience figures for each person. The Portfolio section presents the bottom-up investment philosophy and process, a performance versus volatility chart, sector positions, top holdings, portfolio characteristics and third-quarter trades. A Results section compares annualized and calendar-year performance against the Russell 1000 Value Index, followed by quarter and year-to-date attribution tables. The appendix adds drawdown analysis, dividend sustainability charts, performance expectations, rolling excess returns, biographies, a GIPS composite reference, a glossary and disclosures. The deck closes on the disclosure page. Slide 13 pairs a percentile-ranking chart with a three-metric comparison, slide 30 uses three cumulative performance panels for market-cycle context, and slide 12 lays out the stock selection process as a four-step flow.

decks.title: Sprott Asset Management USA Inc. fund presentation, 2026
decks.summary: The deck opens with a Benjamin Graham quote on businesslike investing, then introduces portfolio manager Jason J. Stevens, CFA, and his background at the firm. It states the strategy's objective of above-average total returns over a five-year-plus horizon and describes a concentrated real asset portfolio built with top-down sector weightings and bottom-up stock selection. The middle sections cover portfolio construction and target exposures across agribusiness, energy and metals/mining, followed by a performance table comparing net and gross returns with three benchmark indices. Current sector weightings and top ten holdings are shown next, then the selection process, investment assessment criteria, and risk management framework. The closing slides cover the firm's overall assets under management, contact details, and a long disclosure page. Slides worth studying include the performance table on slide 8, which pairs fund and index rows in a single grid, and the sector exposure breakdown on slide 7, which lists sub-sectors under each target range.

decks.title: Mitsui Chemicals, Inc. strategy presentation, 2025
decks.summary: This Business Strategy Presentation from Mitsui Chemicals, dated December 17, 2025, is a set of three business-sector strategy talks given by division presidents. It opens with a title slide listing the three sectors: Life & Healthcare Solutions, Mobility Solutions and ICT Solutions. Each sector follows the same sequence: a presenter introduction, a summary slide tying strategy to FY28 and FY30 targets, then detailed sections on sub-businesses. The Life & Healthcare section covers vision care, agrochemicals, oral care and testing/diagnosis. The Mobility section covers elastomers, composite materials and solutions and new business. The ICT section covers semiconductor and assembly, imaging, converting and EUV pellicles. The deck closes with a slide stating a vision to be a global solutions company and a standard disclaimer on forward-looking statements. Slides worth studying include the FY19 to FY30 strategy timeline on slide 3, which combines a bar chart with an annotated history of investments, and the Kulzer restructuring waterfall on slide 9, which pairs a bubble chart of ROIC against invested capital.

decks.title: Verallia strategy presentation, 2021
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide and an agenda naming the presenting executives, then introduces Verallia as a global glass packaging maker, covering its end-market split, footprint, values and purpose. It moves through a materiality exercise and the company's membership in the Ellen MacArthur Foundation. The main body covers the three CSR pillars in order: enhancing the circularity of glass packaging (cullet collection, recycling capacity and furnace use, plus reuse), significantly reducing CO2 emissions (the 2030 target, the levers to reach it, green electricity, lightweighting and tree planting), and providing a safe and inclusive workplace (accident frequency, diversity, employee shareholding and community support). Governance follows, covering board composition, committees, ESG oversight, executive pay, compliance, whistleblowing and responsible purchasing. The deck closes with a conclusion summarizing the ESG ambition and ratings, then a Q&A slide and appendices with the goal tables and historical data. Slides that show the approach well include the CO2 reduction action plan waterfall, the green electricity target chart and the safety roadmap maturity ladder.

decks.title: HSBC Holdings plc strategy presentation, 2018
decks.summary: The deck is HSBC's June 2018 strategy update for investors. It opens with a title slide and a formal notice covering forward-looking statements and non-GAAP measures, then gives a one-page summary of the strategy. The deck moves through four main sections: a profile of the bank as a leading international bank with access to high-growth markets and a strong balance sheet; a review of the transformation since 2011 and the plan for growth in Asia, the US, the UK and transaction banking; the financial framework covering costs, investment of USD15-17bn to 2020, capital and dividends; and a closing conclusion. It closes by restating the target of a return on tangible equity above 11% by 2020 with positive adjusted jaws. Slides worth studying include the strategy summary grid, the market-share charts that pair data with short claims, the wealth-in-Asia breakdown, and the capital bridge that separates the stated target from the underlying drivers. The deck uses dense tables, numbered priority codes that recur across slides, and consistent before-and-after charts to link each initiative to a measurable outcome.

decks.title: Dai-ichi Life Holdings, Inc. strategy presentation, 2026
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide for a business strategy presentation dated January 20, 2026, followed by an agenda that splits the session into two parts: the Protection Business (Japan), led by Kohei Kai, and the Retirement, Savings and Asset Management Business, led by Takashi Iida, each with its own Q&A. Kai's speaker profile comes next, then the Part I content runs through market positioning, the integrated value approach to protection and asset formation, and group company profiles. Later sections cover the sales representative channel, initiatives for sustainable growth and SME expansion, operational efficiency and productivity, the B2B2C business model, sales rep retention and productivity trends, and a product development timeline. The deck closes with a forward-looking statements disclaimer and investor contact details, plus a glossary of group company abbreviations. Slides worth studying are the market chart on slide 5, which pairs ANP figures with a multi-year trend, and the dense timeline on slide 13, which maps products to life stages across two axes. The layouts rely on bold headline figures, tabular comparisons and labeled diagrams.

decks.title: Deutsche Hospitality sales deck, 2022
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide and a short statement that Deutsche Hospitality delights guests with German hospitality worldwide, followed by a logo grid of its brands. It then traces the company's history on a timeline, from the first Steigenberger hotel in 1930 through acquisitions, the Huazhu ownership change and the 2021 rebrand, and presents key facts on hotel count, rooms, countries and turnover. Destination maps show current property locations and planned openings. Next comes a section on the parent Huazhu group, followed by a brand scale matrix that places each brand by price tier and service type. Brand pages follow, each with a photo collage, a one-line positioning and four brand pillars, covering luxury, lifestyle, upscale, midscale and economy brands. A COVID-19 safety section and a loyalty programme overview come before individual hotel pages with key facts, location and benefits. The deck closes with a contact page and a thank-you slide.

decks.title: CrossCheck sales deck
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide reading CrossCheck, Your Partner in Payment Processing, then introduces the company on a slide that pairs three benefit headings (Increase Sales, Mitigate Risk, Save Time and Money) with a short About Us paragraph describing its payment guarantee services for merchants of all sizes. A slide on the guarantee factor explains what the guarantee covers, followed by a slide that lays out ACH product options such as eCheck, Pay-by-Link and Standing ACH. The middle sections cover check conversion and deposit methods, a security and compliance statement, and supported user interfaces and gateways, including terminal and portal options. The deck closes with an onboarding slide describing a dedicated customer success representative, scheduled trainings and check-in calls, followed by a thank you slide with the company's address in Petaluma, California. Slides worth studying include the benefit-heading layout on slide 2, the product grid on slide 4 and the process-flow style of slide 5.

decks.title: Marina Bay Sands conference talk, 2023
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide reading Sustainable Events at Marina Bay Sands, then sets out the property's sustainability journey from 2011 to 2022 as a timeline. It moves to the key sustainability focus areas (climate response, water stewardship, waste and circularity, sustainable sourcing, biodiversity, and culture and capacity building), followed by the 2023 sustainability goals grouped by category. Later sections cover the carbon neutral venue status, triple platinum certifications, responsible seafood, regional sourcing, sustainable menu options such as plant-based meat, and circularity examples such as upcycled table numbers and menu cubes. A section on event communication shows how planners can display sustainability commitments through speeches, factsheets, menus and physical or digital signage. The deck closes with an impact statement listing partnerships with WWF Singapore, The Food Bank Singapore and Seven Clean Seas, sustainability videos, and a thank you slide. Slides 4, 5 and 6 are good examples of dense data presented in a clear grid, and slides 8 and 9 to 14 show a consistent format of a headline, a supporting line and image-led panels.

decks.title: Complynet sales deck, 2022
decks.summary: The deck is a sales presentation from Complynet, a compliance provider for automotive dealers, branded for 700Credit and dated July 2022 on its title slide. It opens with Complynet's company history and then turns to the FTC Safeguards Rule, covering its original 2003 effective date, the October 2021 revision, the December 9, 2022 enforcement date for new provisions, and the penalty amount. The core of the deck walks through ten required compliance steps in order: establishing a safeguards team, written risk assessment, written information security program, information security training, phishing penetration testing, vendor assessments and agreements, access controls, technical requirements, written incident response plan, and written annual report to the board. Each step is shown with a repeated navigation graphic that tracks progress through the sequence, and most steps list the specific tasks involved. The closing section compares Complynet's offerings with those of other providers, listing which documents and services Complynet creates or performs versus those the dealer must build from templates, and ends with a contact slide for 700Credit.

decks.title: Rise AV sales deck, 2026
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide reading "Closing the Skills Gap. Empowering Women in AV" and sponsorship opportunities for 2026. It then sets out the problem: the AV sector is ageing and underrepresents women, with women making up 9% of the workforce and 2% of technical roles, against a projected 2.3 million skilled worker shortfall. Next it presents Rise AV's goals and its five pillars of career paths, training, community, representation and corporate work. The middle sections describe the Mentoring and Elevate programmes, with outcome statistics from mentee follow-ups, and make the case that investing in women leaders benefits employers. A slide on what is coming in 2026 comes next, followed by the benefits of sponsorship, the sponsorship tiers from regional to global headline partner, and a table of what each tier includes. The deck closes with ways to support the organisation and a contact page. Slides 6 and 13 are the most worth studying: the first pairs each outcome figure with a single label, and the second uses a compact tier table to compare packages side by side.

decks.title: Intel sales deck, 2022
decks.summary: This sales deck introduces the 4th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors and the Intel Xeon CPU Max Series. It opens with a headline slide of performance claims across general compute, AI, 5G vRAN, data analytics, HPC, and networking and storage, then repeats that summary with power and emissions figures. The middle sections cover the platform in detail: architecture and die packaging, memory and interconnect specifications, the built-in accelerators (AMX, DSA, IAA, DLB, QAT), and the security features. Later sections present workload benchmarks against the 3rd Gen parts, a fleet-level total cost of ownership comparison, a high-bandwidth-memory section, and customer quotes. The deck closes with a summary of its claims, a product comparison table, and extensive benchmark configuration notes in the backup. Most slides are dense with footnoted test results, and the layout relies on bar charts and tables. Slides worth studying are the opening overview, the die-package comparison, the accelerator benefit slides, and the TCO table, which lays out assumptions side by side.

decks.title: Black Lake Capital sales deck, 2025
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide introducing Black Lake Capital as a strategic investment firm and family office focused on technology-driven, middle-market companies. It then covers the firm's mission and vision, followed by its core values of compassion, commitment, and collaboration. The investment philosophy section lists four principles: empowering founders, maximizing returns, leading in technology, and accelerating impact. The offering section describes capital for growth, add-on acquisitions, operational support, and tech market expertise. Three portfolio case studies follow, covering Spinnaker SCA, Set Solutions SSI, and A5 Consultants, each with a company profile, strategic actions, and key measures of success. The team section introduces the managing partner, partner, advisory board members, and their backgrounds. The deck closes with a call to action and contact details. The slides are built as dense, text-heavy layouts with numbered points and consistent case study templates, which makes the portfolio section easy to compare across companies. The portfolio slides and the team slide are the most useful to study for structure.

decks.title: Troutwood product launch, 2024
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide, "A Financial Plan For Life," and a definition of a financial plan as a way to set goals, follow a path and adjust as events occur. It then makes a case for financial literacy through three trends: micro investing, financial literacy classes in schools and financial wellness in the workplace. Next it covers long-term investing with a compounding return chart and three investment lessons for educators. A problem section cites statistics on teen employment, paycheck-to-paycheck living and low financial literacy, followed by a solution section presenting the Troutwood app and its three-step plan builder (profile, career, goal). The app section includes a green-shield likelihood and adequacy indicator and download instructions. The deck closes with educator support tools, a financial plan message, and a stock market simulation game called Buy, Sell, Hold! plus an interactive stock market map. Slides 4, 13 and 12 are the most worth studying for their visual design.

decks.title: LOGOTORU sales deck
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide and table of contents, then moves through four parts: what the client hands off, why a stop line matters, what LOGOTORU OS shows, and what the client has at month six. It first describes the four deliverables (execution, observation design, population definition and a monthly decision report) and a six-month plan split into design, launch, run and decide phases. A customer-voices slide and a track-record section follow, with ORIT's summary marked as the company's own account rather than a quote. Next comes the problem framing: enterprise outbound tends to push without a defined stop threshold, the target list is finite, and negative responses are hard to reverse. Charts on burnout indicators support this argument. The product section shows the manager view, operator view and decision log with screenshots, then a month-six deliverables slide and an illustrative ROI slide marked as hypothetical. A comparison table with alternatives, a FAQ, pricing, founder background and contact details close the deck, with a final call to book a consultation.

decks.title: Maki People sales deck, 2025
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide labeled as a 2025 sales deck, then presents its pitch: fully autonomous AI HR agents that handle sourcing, screening and interviewing at scale. It next addresses the problem, arguing that ATS and LMS tools leave HR teams stuck with manual screening, scheduling and interviewing, and that much talent data is unstructured. The solution section explains that the agents can be customized to a company's workflows and branding, run voice, video or text interviews, and rank candidates. A slide on skills and role coverage follows, then a section on fairness and compliance that cites psychometric development and the New York City LL144 rule. Outcome metrics come next, followed by a customer case study on a global fashion retailer, presented across two identical slides. The deck closes with a forward-looking vision of agents that manage workforce planning, followed by a call to schedule a demo and contact details.

decks.title: Cisco sales deck
decks.summary: The deck is a partner sales presentation from Cisco about its joint go-to-market work with Microsoft. It opens with the title slide and a framing slide that positions Cisco and Microsoft together for cloud, AI, security and hybrid work, then makes a case for why the two companies partner. Next it covers the Cisco advantage, pairing integrated networking, security, observability and collaboration with Splunk analytics, and then explains how partners can sell through the Azure Marketplace using Multiparty Private Offers and Reseller Enabled Offers. A product map follows, grouping offerings by workplace, data center, assurance, security and digital resilience, and a slide shows Cisco Devices for Microsoft Teams Rooms. A Splunk section explains how customers can buy through the marketplace against their Microsoft commitments. The deck closes with customer outcome figures, a partnership summary and a closing call to action. Slides are dense with bullet text and labelled navigation tabs repeat across the footer of each page.

decks.title: Avient investor presentation, 2024
decks.summary: The deck opens with a welcome slide and an agenda naming the presenters, followed by a forward-looking statements disclaimer and non-GAAP measures notice. The strategic overview comes next, covering the company's purpose, its growth framework of catalyzing the core and building new platforms of scale, and four strategic drivers: portfolio prioritization, amplified innovation, digital for operational excellence, and leadership and culture. Segment reviews follow for Color, Additives and Inks and for Specialty Engineered Materials, each giving an overview, end markets, addressable market sizes, and margin expansion levers. A spotlight on advanced composites comes next. The financial section covers sustainability commitments, long-term targets for organic growth and a path to 20%+ adjusted EBITDA margins, capital allocation priorities, and an investment summary. The deck closes with a reconciliation table of non-GAAP figures. Slides that show the structure well include the framework diagram on slide 10, the segment margin bridges on slides 36 and 51, and the consolidated margin bridge on slide 58.

decks.title: Citi investor presentation, 2026
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide for Shahmir Khaliq, Head of Services, and a Services overview covering Investor Services, Treasury and Trade Solutions and Liquidity Management, with headline network and scale figures. It then shows performance against targets through market share and financial charts, followed by a page on how Services stays resilient through rate cycles, supported by client relationships and fee drivers. Next come industry trends and the strategy's key focus areas, a slide on growth by client segment and vertical, and sections on next-generation platforms, AI initiatives, innovative solutions and digital asset strategy. A slide sets out near-term and through-the-cycle return targets, a forward-looking statements disclaimer follows, and footnotes for each slide close the deck. Slides worth studying include slide 3, which pairs multi-year bar charts with market share callouts, slide 4, which links rate charts to fee and deposit drivers, slide 7, which uses large metric tiles for platform outcomes, and slide 11, which lays out returns trajectory against key drivers.

decks.title: Accenture investor presentation, 2026
decks.summary: The deck is an investor day presentation dated October 14, 2026, from Accenture. It opens with a full-year FY26 results slide comparing guidance with actual revenue growth, adjusted EPS, operating margin, cash returned to shareholders and free cash flow. A short section follows that reviews FY22 to FY26 performance, including revenue, EPS, margin and capital deployed. The middle of the deck covers capital allocation, the FY27 to FY29 ambition with targets for growth, margin and cash returns, and a breakdown of the business by industry, service type and region. Further slides explain how the company invests in pricing, delivery and talent, and describe its acquisition strategy and inorganic contribution. The deck closes with a list of long-term measures of growth, followed by an appendix of GAAP to non-GAAP reconciliations, a free cash flow table, people metrics and a forward-looking statements disclaimer. Slide 2 is a dense scorecard that sets actuals against original guidance. Slide 5 lays out the three-year ambition in a grid. Slide 10 pairs acquisition spending with a bar view of inorganic contribution by year.

decks.title: ADI Global Distribution Inc. investor presentation, 2026
decks.summary: The deck opens with a cover slide for the 2026 Investor Day, followed by a forward-looking statements disclaimer and a day agenda listing speakers from the CEO, merchandising, digital, operations and finance. The company is introduced as the spin-off of ADI from Resideo, a specialty distributor of low-voltage products, with standalone FY2025 revenue and adjusted EBITDA shown beside the building products company being spun off. The strategy section sets out four pillars: category leadership, an omnichannel platform, multiple growth levers and margin upside. Subsequent sections cover the products and suppliers offer, the omnichannel customer experience, operations and trusted partner service, and financial performance. The financial section presents historical results, 2030 targets, capital allocation and pro forma capitalization. The appendix reconciles non-GAAP EBITDA figures. Slides worth studying include the strategy overview on slide 6, the revenue and M&A growth chart on slide 9, and the digital growth algorithm on slide 42.

decks.title: Brookfield Asset Management investor presentation, 2026
decks.summary: The deck is an investor day presentation from Brookfield Asset Management, dated to mid-2026 based on data as of June 30, 2026. It opens with a title slide and an agenda listing speakers including the CEO, CFO, and the Co-CEO of Credit, followed by a section titled The Brookfield Advantage. The middle sections cover the firm's business mix across five groups, its consistency of performance, its positioning for future trends, and its growth model. The CFO section explains the company's structure and projects fee-bearing capital, fee-related earnings and distributable earnings through 2031. A credit section then covers the platform after the Oaktree integration, the market environment, and the main growth areas. The deck closes with key takeaways, a CEO panel slide, and endnotes and notices. Worth studying: slide 4, which packs headline capital figures for each business group into one view; slide 24, a table comparing target and actual returns across strategies; slide 46, a bar chart with a record-year callout; and slide 91, which uses a simple Treasury yield line to frame the credit market shift.

decks.title: Pershing Square Holdings, Ltd. fund presentation, 2025
decks.summary: The deck is the annual investor presentation for Pershing Square Holdings, Ltd. (PSH), dated February 11, 2025. It opens with a title slide and a long disclaimer on performance, risk and the limits of the analysis. The agenda then runs through a chairman's introduction, the board of directors and its process, and a strategic update covering the debt financing strategy, performance against the discount to NAV, the PSCM stake sale, the postponed PSUS IPO, and a proposed transaction with Howard Hughes Holdings. A 2024 performance review follows, with long-run return tables, a contributors and detractors breakdown, and assets under management. The business update covers market concentration, index inclusion and the investment team. The equity portfolio section closes the deck with one slide per major holding. Slides worth studying include the debt maturity and leverage chart, the net-return comparison tables, and the contributors and detractors tables, which show how gross and net figures are set side by side.

decks.title: Events.com investor presentation, 2024
decks.summary: This August 2024 investor presentation, prepared for the proposed business combination between Concord Acquisition Corp II and Events.com, Inc., opens with a title slide and then a long disclaimer covering forward-looking statements, the proposed transaction and securities-law notices. It introduces the SPAC team and its investing experience, then moves to the company: a category-defining domain name, key investment highlights and a brand-value slide built on domain purchase prices. The core company section describes the problem of fragmented event tools, the unified platform as the solution, company metrics and a management and investor roster. A product section walks through creator tools (sell, sponsor, promote, execute, insights) and the Discover consumer recommendation engine. Market sizing, business model and key metrics follow, then transaction overview and a dense risk-factor section. The deck closes on the risk factors rather than a call to action. Slides worth studying include the problem-to-solution sequence on slides 11 and 12, the market-size comparison on slide 34 and the sources-and-uses table on slide 41.

decks.title: Fox Corporation and Roku, Inc. presentation, 2026
decks.summary: The deck is an investor presentation dated June 15, 2026, announcing Fox's proposed acquisition of Roku. It opens with a title slide and then a long disclaimer covering forward-looking statements, non-GAAP measures, transaction filing information, participants in the solicitation and a no-offer statement. The substance begins with a transaction overview listing consideration of 60 percent cash and 40 percent stock, implied equity and enterprise values, ownership split, leverage, synergies and expected closing timing. The middle sections frame the strategic rationale through industry shifts toward live sports and news and the rise of streaming, a combined-company profile, Roku's business model and growth metrics, and high-growth advertising and subscription verticals. Further slides cover audience reach and engagement, advertising engine economics, pro forma revenue mix, and financial attributes. The deck closes with a sources and uses table and transaction details. Slides 3, 5 and 8 are worth studying for how they pair headline numbers with source notes and labeled business-model diagrams, and slide 14 for how it lays out a sources and uses table alongside transaction bullets.

decks.title: TD Bank Group investor presentation, 2026
decks.summary: This is TD Bank Group's Q1 2026 investor presentation, opening with a forward-looking statements caution and a title slide, then a snapshot of the bank's businesses, national ranking and the Q1 2026 performance figures. The middle sections cover the four business lines and their F'26 strategic priorities, cost reduction and restructuring, the U.S. BSA/AML remediation, AI initiatives and digital engagement. Credit is the largest block, with allowance and impairment trends, provision ratios by segment, and detail on Canadian residential real estate lending, commercial lending and U.S. personal and commercial portfolios. Later sections address capital and CET1 movements, TLAC, liquidity, funding, credit ratings, covered bonds, bail-in and NVCC loss absorption, and interest rate sensitivity. The appendix covers economic outlook and interest rate views, followed by endnotes defining non-GAAP measures and footnotes for each slide. The deck is built as a dense, data-heavy sequence of tables and charts with a consistent slide header and repeated forward-looking disclaimers.

decks.title: Sunoco LP investor presentation, 2025
decks.summary: The deck opens with a standard forward-looking statements disclaimer and non-GAAP definitions, followed by investor relations contacts. It then moves into an investment overview covering the Parkland acquisition, the company's scale across fuel distribution and energy infrastructure, its balance sheet and distribution policy, and a structure chart for the Sunoco LP and SunocoCorp LLC entities. Next comes a section on distribution per unit growth and total return compared with the S&P 500 and midstream peers. The business segments section follows, covering fuel distribution, terminals, pipeline systems and the integrated refinery and marketing system, each with market context and performance charts. The deck then turns to future growth, including a timeline of acquisitions since 2018, a bolt-on strategy for fuel distribution, geographic growth priorities and a closing slide on midstream acquisition multiples. Its visual approach relies on bold section dividers, dense bullet text, and charts that pair company metrics with industry benchmarks.

decks.title: Versigent investor presentation, 2026
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide naming CEO Joe Liotine and CFO Doug Ostermann, followed by forward-looking statement and non-GAAP disclaimers. It then moves into a business overview with key metrics on revenue, end markets and regions, and a one-slide investment thesis. The middle sections cover the company's electrical architecture product portfolio, its proprietary engineering tool suite, the engineering and manufacturing model, and the supply chain. Next come industry dynamics, including secular trends and content-per-vehicle growth, and a financials overview with a 2026 to 2028 framework and 2026 guidance. The closing slide summarizes the value-creation case, and the appendix holds presenter bios and non-GAAP reconciliations. The deck is built around dense data callouts with footnoted sourcing, and it uses a consistent footer on every page. Several slides use a few large figures with short supporting bullets, which makes the key numbers easy to scan. The financial slides pair a revenue bridge and an EBITDA bridge, each showing the 2025 starting point and the 2026 guidance.

decks.title: KfW Bankengruppe investor presentation, 2026
decks.summary: This deck is KfW's semi-annual investor presentation, dated November 2026 with data as of 31 October 2026. It opens with a disclaimer on US securities offers, followed by a table of contents. The business model section covers promotional volumes, the on-lending model, exposure by region and sector, and Frankfurt as a financial hub. Next, rating and funding cover the federal guarantee, financial and ESG ratings, and debt capital markets by currency and product. Later sections address sustainability, including SDG mapping, green bond allocation and impact, and digitalisation initiatives such as DLT-based bonds. The Germany Fund is also presented. The appendix contains the worldwide office network, liquidity portfolio, strategic holdings, key IFRS figures, Nordic and Asian funding, and sustainability governance. The deck closes with contact details and a photo credits slide. Several slides are dense tables of funding data and benchmark issues, serving as a reference for how an issuer lays out financial information. Slides 5 and 10 present key metrics as headline figures with short explanations, while slide 14 organises a long list of external ratings by agency and outlook.

decks.title: Host Hotels & Resorts investor presentation, 2026
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide reading Investor Presentation, dated November 2026, followed by forward-looking statement and non-GAAP disclaimers and a table of contents. Its main sections run in order: Company Overview, Recent Highlights, Portfolio Update, Growth Opportunities, Corporate Responsibility, and Reconciliations and Supplemental Information. The company overview uses a fact sheet with pie charts for brand, chain scale, manager and business mix, a top-10 markets list, and a comparison against other full-service lodging REITs. Recent highlights cover Q3 2026 results, a full-year 2026 outlook table, and acquisition slides for two hotels, each with a rationale list and a property overview. The portfolio update covers rate-driven revenue growth, group and transient demand, and a capital allocation summary. Growth opportunities detail renovation programs with Marriott and Hyatt and a capex summary table. Corporate responsibility closes the main body with climate, sustainability and governance pages. Slides 5, 9 and 22 are good models for dense data layout, and slides 18 and 28 for tabular comparisons.

decks.title: Cloudflare, Inc. investor presentation, 2026
decks.summary: The deck is Cloudflare's investor presentation as of June 30, 2026, and opens with a safe harbor disclosure covering forward-looking statements and non-GAAP measures. It then moves to a company overview with a mission slide and an at-a-glance page of key figures such as large customers, revenue, and network reach. The middle sections describe a single programmable network and composable platform, how the company's product and network flywheels work, a growing total addressable market, and a case for AI and agents as a new demand driver, including a proposed market structure for metered agent activity. The financial section covers the business model, revenue and customer growth, dollar-based net retention, unit economics, operating expense leverage, cash position, Q3 and full-year guidance, and a long-term operating model with a GAAP profitability target. It closes with the appendix containing the GAAP to non-GAAP reconciliation, key business metric tables, and definitions and Gartner sources. Slides worth studying include the single-platform diagram on slide 9, the revenue and customer growth chart on slide 35, and the unit economics explanation on slide 38.

decks.title: WaFd, Inc. and EverBank Financial Corp pitch deck, 2026
decks.company: WaFd, Inc. and EverBank Financial Corp
decks.summary: The deck is an investor presentation for WaFd's proposed merger with EverBank, dated September 7, 2026. It opens with a title slide and then a long forward-looking statements disclaimer and a note on presenters, followed by a transaction overview that sets out the combined bank's scale, multi-channel model and key deal terms such as the 100% stock structure, ownership split and anticipated 1Q'27 close. The middle sections cover the financial rationale, including EPS accretion, cost synergies, integration timeline, capital and liquidity, credit quality, and value creation scenarios based on price-to-tangible-book comparisons. Standalone profiles of EverBank's regional, national and digital channels, its deposit franchise and its management team follow in the main body. The appendix holds detailed channel descriptions, loan and deposit mix, non-depository and commercial real estate exposure, tangible book value and goodwill reconciliations, and the EPS accretion calculation. The deck ends with a closing slide reading Stronger Together. Several slides, including the channel mix and purchase accounting pages, show how complex financial data is laid out for an investor audience.

decks.title: Wayfair investor presentation, 2025
decks.summary: The deck is Wayfair's 2025 investor presentation, dated February 20, 2025, and opens with a forward-looking statements safe harbor before a contents page. It then moves through four main sections: the Home category, where the company sizes the market and describes how home shopping differs from search-based retail; competitive advantages, covering brand reach, the CastleGate logistics network, speed-driven conversion, a cost markup model, product range, the Wayfair Verified curation label, a membership program, customer service and generative AI; growth initiatives, including Wayfair Professional, a luxury brand push, international expansion into Canada, the UK and Ireland, physical stores and advertising; and financials, covering revenue and orders, gross margin, fixed cost discipline, capital structure and a stepped path toward 10% adjusted EBITDA margin. An appendix defines the non-GAAP measures used. The deck closes on the margin roadmap and the appendix. Slides worth studying include the speed badge conversion chart, the CastleGate comparison, the Wayfair Verified performance slide, and the multi-step profitability roadmap.

decks.title: Givaudan investor presentation, 2026
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide and a short 'Who we are' section covering Givaudan's brand video, global footprint of production sites, creation centres, locations and employees, and a split of sales across its Taste & Wellbeing and Fragrance & Beauty businesses. It then moves through each business in turn, showing product categories, growth drivers to 2030, differentiated solutions and commercial strategy, followed by a 'How we do it' section on customer success, the research-driven innovation process and future-proofing through digital tools. A strategy section sets out the 2030 targets, growth drivers and purpose ambitions for nature, people and communities. The financial part reviews performance across the 2021 to 2025 cycle, half-year 2026 results, dividend history, debt maturities and the 2026 outlook. Governance pages introduce the Executive Committee and Board, and a reporting section and disclaimer close the deck. Slides worth studying include the sales-mix slide with its repeated tiles, the business-activity slides that pair a product list with a short positioning line, and the long-run dividend and free cash flow bar chart.

decks.title: BMW Group investor presentation, 2026
decks.summary: This investor relations deck from BMW Group, dated November 2026, opens with a title slide and then sets out a vision of premium individual mobility. Its strategy rests on brands, powertrains, technology and people, and sustainability. The middle sections cover the Neue Klasse platform, the battery and Gen6 roadmap, a software-defined vehicle and AI architecture, and factory and supply chain setup, with the global footprint and charging network shown on regional maps. A sustainability block follows, covering the net zero path to 2050, renewable energy at plants, supply chain decarbonisation and the iX3 product footprint. The financial section comes last, covering sales, segment EBIT margins, Financial Services, funding, treasury, capex, R&D, free cash flow, dividends and share buybacks, followed by the 2026 outlook. The deck closes with investor relations contacts, the 2027 financial calendar, a forward-looking statements disclaimer and consumption and emission data. Slides worth studying include the Neue Klasse quantum-leap slide, the layered SDV versus AI-defined vehicle diagram on slide 26, and the segment EBIT chart on slide 45.

decks.title: Owens Corning investor presentation, 2026
decks.summary: This Q1 2026 investor presentation from Owens Corning opens with a title slide listing the investor conferences where it was shared, followed by forward-looking statements and non-GAAP disclaimers. It then introduces the company as a building products leader with three businesses (Roofing, Insulation and Doors), shows revenue by end market and geography, and compares its adjusted EBITDA margin with peers and against housing and shingle market data. Next come margin assumptions by segment, strategic priorities and financial targets through 2028, and capital allocation and capex plans. Segment sections for Roofing, Insulation and Doors follow, covering market position, secular trends and cost initiatives, with appendices holding market data, key financial tables, revenue disaggregation and non-GAAP reconciliations. The deck closes with reconciliation tables rather than a call to action. Slides worth studying include the peer margin comparison on slide 4, which pairs company and peer data on one chart, the margin-versus-macro overlay on slide 5, the strategic priorities and targets layout on slide 7, and the cash flow and capital allocation charts on slides 10 and 11.

decks.title: Novartis investor presentation, 2026
decks.summary: The deck is Novartis's Q3 2026 results investor presentation, dated October 27, 2026, and presented by CEO Vas Narasimhan and CFO Mukul Mehta. It opens with a title slide and a forward-looking statements disclaimer, then moves through a sequence of sections: company overview, financial review, innovation and pipeline, conclusions, and a large appendix. The company overview covers Q3 sales growth, core margin expansion, and sales tables for priority brands such as Kisqali, Kesimpta, Pluvicto, Leqvio, Scemblix, Cosentyx and Rhapsido, each with a slide of quarterly charts and market-share commentary. The financial review presents key figures, capital allocation, the raised full-year core operating income guidance, a quarterly growth outlook and a currency impact slide. The innovation section reports readouts for remibrutinib, del-desiran and pelacarsen, followed by a pipeline overview and a detailed appendix of clinical trial summaries. The deck closes with conclusions and an upcoming investor event. Slides worth studying include the Q3 headline summary, which pairs bar charts with a short list of pipeline highlights, and the Kisqali slide, which combines a monthly NBRx trend line with a competitor comparison.

decks.title: Pershing Square Holdings, Ltd. fund presentation, 2026
decks.summary: The deck is the annual investor presentation of Pershing Square Holdings, Ltd. (PSH), dated February 11, 2026, and covers its 2025 results. It opens with a title slide and a disclaimer on performance, risk and the limits of forward-looking statements. The agenda then moves through a chairman's introduction, a board overview, a strategic update covering debt financing, the discount to NAV, the PSUS listing and the HHH transaction, followed by a 2025 performance review with annual and cumulative return tables and contributor and detractor breakdowns. Next come a business and organizational update, a market developments section on valuation and earnings growth since COVID, and an equity portfolio update covering holdings such as Brookfield, Uber, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, Amazon and Universal Music Group. The deck closes with an organizational update and team profiles. Slides worth studying include the contributor and detractor slides, which use a consistent layout for gross attribution, and the position-by-position slides, which pair a share price chart with dated event markers and a stated average cost.

decks.title: b.fab pitch deck, 2024
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide introducing circular biomanufacturing based on liquid feedstocks, followed by a framing of the problem: fossil-based chemicals and animal-based products carry heavy CO2 and land-use costs. It then presents b.fab's solution, a proprietary process that turns industrial CO2, biomass waste and sidestreams into formate, methanol, hydrogen and protein, fatty acids and amino acids. Market sections size the opportunity from a global animal feed total down to a European salmon feed protein gap, and describe aquaculture as the beachhead market. Further slides cover the product pipeline, technology and IP, customer traction, the licensing and joint venture business model, a roadmap across technology readiness levels, the team and advisors, and a financial projection with unit economics. The deck closes with the seed ask of 2.5 million euros, its use of funds across go-to-market, team and scale-up, and contact details. Slides worth studying include the market sizing funnel on slide 8, the side-by-side sustainability comparison on slide 10, and the revenue and unit economics slide on slide 14.

decks.title: Cube pitch deck
decks.summary: The deck opens with a founder note from Christina Ross, CEO and co-founder, who describes her frustration as a former CFO with slow, consultant-dependent FP&A tools. A short company snapshot follows, listing the founding year, headquarters, employee count, funding and backers. The middle section frames the problem: finance teams are shifting toward strategic roles while their tools lag, and they feel forced to choose between manual spreadsheets and disruptive rip-and-replace systems. Several slides cite the claim that most teams who replace spreadsheets revert to them. The product section presents Cube as a spreadsheet-native FP&A platform built on Excel and Google Sheets, shows a three-step workflow of connecting data, integrating into spreadsheets and pivoting analysis, and notes a short go-live time. Customer logos and an ARR growth slide follow, then a market slide describing a large untapped opportunity. The deck closes with a call to join the company's approach to FP&A.

decks.title: Sharper Sense pitch deck, 2020
decks.summary: The deck opens with the company name and a title slide, then states the problem: impaired sensory processing from aging, neurological disorders, fatigue and injury reduces acuity and raises fall risk. It presents a noninvasive vagus nerve stimulation patch as the solution. Next it explains the mechanism through a brain-pathway diagram, lists the drawbacks of alternatives such as stimulants, nootropics and therapy, and cites the academic papers behind the approach. The product section covers form factor, features and target price, followed by a competitor comparison table of VNS devices by application, form factor and stimulation location. The deck then describes the consumer impact of age-related sensory decline and sizes adjacent markets. A revenue and gross margin projection table from 2024 to 2029 is followed by a regulatory and reimbursement plan, expansion markets, a timeline of research, funding and milestones, a proposed pilot study, the founding team and partner institutions. It closes with a seed round ask of $400K and contact details.

decks.title: Seedcamp fund presentation, 2025
decks.summary: The deck is a fundraising presentation from the venture firm Seedcamp, seeking investment for its Seedcamp VII (Core) and Seedcamp Nation II (Select) funds. It opens with a title slide and a headline on backing European tech founders, then lists the two fund offerings with their target sizes. The main sections follow in order: The Seedcamp Advantage (history, performance and team), The Seedcamp Way (sourcing, selecting and winning, supporting, and driving returns), and the fund strategies with their thesis, ticket sizes, ownership targets and follow-on reserves for each fund. The deck closes with a short call to join the Seedcamp Nation. Slides worth studying include the performance table comparing fund vintages, the power-law returns breakdown by outcome bucket, the sourcing channel slide showing how deals arrive, and the side-by-side fund strategy comparison. Several slides use compact tables and short labelled callouts, which make dense fund data easy to scan.

decks.title: Letz!Go pitch deck, 2021
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide presenting Letz!Go as a platform connecting truck owners with B2B cargo owners. It then sets out the problem from both sides: cargo owners struggle to get working capital and depend on brokers, while truck owners find it hard to know truck availability and cannot pay a down payment. Next comes the solution, which has three parts: Letz!Go for matching trucks and cargo on one web platform, Letz!Track for a free transport management system, and Letz!Fund for down payments and payment terms. A market size slide and a four-step process for sending cargo follow, with slides 5 to 10 walking through order confirmation, driver notification, tracking and analytics dashboards. The business model, competitor table, competitive advantages and team slides come next. The deck closes with client and partner logos and contact details. Slides worth studying include the problem slide, the four-step process sequence, and the competitor comparison table.

decks.title: ARC Ento Tech Ltd investor presentation
decks.summary: The deck is a fundraising presentation for ARC Ento Tech Ltd, an Australian company seeking a $10 million Series A raise to fund six commercial plants that convert mixed municipal waste into products. It opens with a call to imagine a future without landfills, followed by an investment summary slide that sets out share price, minimum investment, valuation and projected returns. The middle sections cover the scale of the global waste problem, the market potential, the company's revenue streams and its processing approach. A competitive positioning slide compares its continuous, distributed plants against batch and centralised alternatives, and a social proof slide gathers quotes from customers, officials and third-party research. Leadership and technical advisor profiles follow, and the deck closes with contact details and the line "Work with Nature, Not Against It." Slides worth studying include the investment summary, which packs many figures into one view, the competitive positioning slide with its low-to-high axes, and the social proof slide, which pairs quotes with the source of each claim.

decks.title: BrightView investor presentation, 2025
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide and a forward-looking statements disclaimer, then introduces BrightView as a commercial landscaping and snow services company with about 20,000 employees, $2.8B in revenue and 280 branch locations. It moves through the company's history, showing a prior period of revenue growth without profit growth, the refreshed focus under new leadership, and the 2023 to 2025 adjusted EBITDA trend. Core sections cover the market opportunity, frontline employee turnover, customer retention, development-business growth, share of wallet, national accounts, capital allocation, and a path to about $4B in revenue and 16%+ EBITDA margins by 2030. Operational levers follow, including purchasing, fleet management, and SG&A rebalancing toward sales. The appendix holds FY25 guidance, leadership, and non-GAAP reconciliations. The deck closes with a short thank-you slide. Slides worth studying are the customer retention and turnover correlation charts on slides 22 and 23, which pair a single metric with a clear visual, and the revenue bridge on slide 33 that breaks growth into labeled drivers.

decks.title: Key Venture presentation, 2023
decks.summary: The deck is a corporate profile from Key Venture, a financial services firm that advises early and growth stage startups on raising capital. It opens with a title slide and an offering statement describing the firm's advisory and fund management arms. The middle sections cover the services offered (transaction advisory, fund management and portfolio management, with stage, ticket size and investor targets for each), the reasons to choose the firm, and its step-by-step approach to investment advisory across seven stages. It then presents deal metrics, investor coverage, lists of investors in recent transactions, the core team and advisors, a set of deal credentials, detailed case studies, and client testimonials. It closes with contact details for the two founders. Slides worth studying include the services overview on slide 3, which uses a consistent three-column layout for each service line, the process diagram on slide 5, and the case study template on slide 21, which lays out deal value, service, investors, industry and date in a grid before the narrative sections.

decks.title: Neutonic pitch deck, 2026
decks.summary: The deck opens with a private and confidential investment proposal dated January 2026, then frames a gap in the market for focus-enhancing products beyond caffeine. It introduces Neutonic as a nootropic brand and presents its traction: cases sold, revenue since November 2023, subscriber numbers and channel and location splits. Next come the founding team and creator partners, the product lineup and key ingredient blend, and a 2026 launch plan with a product roadmap. Several slides show launch campaigns, customer reviews, and margin and cost improvements. The deck then covers UK and USA retail rollout progress, revenue projections, the funding round terms with an illustrative investor return table, a valuation rationale based on revenue multiples, investment objectives, and market growth data. It closes with a future-acquisition section naming possible buyers and recent deals, followed by thank-you and appendix slides with product details, pricing, the clinical science behind each ingredient, a market map, and customer profiles. Several slides are worth studying for how they are built, including the product comparison map and the ingredient science slides.

decks.title: Aerbio investor presentation, 2024
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide and then a page of investment disclaimers and representations that an investor must accept, followed by the company's one-line mission of turning carbon dioxide into protein with microbes. It then moves through the problem of rising protein demand and pressure on arable land, the proposed solution of single cell protein (Proton) made from gases, and why the timing is now, linked to the energy transition. Market sizing follows, covering total addressable and serviceable markets, a comparison with peer fermentation approaches, and traction from pilot-scale production and partnerships. Later sections describe the business model (licensing, joint ventures and owned plants), the team and locations, a scale-up roadmap from lab to commercial plants with the Series A funding for a demonstration facility, and a closing list of reasons to invest. The deck ends with contact details. Several slides are dense with tables and bulleted claims, and the market and roadmap slides are the most useful to study for layout and information design.

decks.title: Capsida Biotherapeutics investor presentation, 2025
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide and a forward-looking statements disclaimer, then frames the problem with first-generation genetic medicines: poor blood-brain barrier crossing, liver and dorsal root ganglia toxicity, narrow therapeutic windows, and risky invasive routes of delivery. It presents Capsida as a next-generation genetic medicines company with three wholly-owned programs in CNS and ophthalmology, followed by a pipeline timeline. Each program gets its own section covering the disease opportunity, preclinical non-human primate data on brain expression and liver and DRG detargeting, and the planned clinical study design. A platform section covers capsid engineering, manufacturing capabilities, and a facility overview. The closing sections list leadership and board members, funding history, and contact details, and the deck ends by repeating the company summary from the opening. Slides 8, 9 and 15 are worth studying for how the company charts preclinical expression and detargeting results against a benchmark, and slide 4 for how the pipeline timeline is laid out across programs.

decks.title: MedFire Innovations Inc. investor presentation, 2023
decks.summary: The deck opens with a title slide labeled Exhibit A Pitch Deck, followed by a legal disclaimer and a company origin story. It then moves through the company's culture of innovation, its three divisions (MedFire Innovations, MedFire Jobs and MedFire Expo), the company's assets and intellectual property, and its leadership team and advisors. The middle sections describe who each division serves, what it does, how it operates and how it earns revenue, supported by industry market-size statistics from IBISWorld. Near the end, the deck turns to a crowdfunding offer of 100,000 shares of Series A Preferred Stock at $10 per share, with a $1,000,000 total offering, a $500 minimum investment and a 6 percent cumulative yearly dividend. It closes with contact details and the company's San Diego address. Slides worth studying include the three-division layout on slide 6, the process diagram on slide 16 and the investment terms on slides 35 and 36.

decks.title: California Child Care Resource & Referral Network product launch
decks.company: California Child Care Resource & Referral Network
decks.summary: The deck opens with a problem statement: online child care searches are confusing, hard to compare, and may not be reliable. It then introduces MyChildCarePlan.org as a state-funded, no-cost consumer education tool available in four languages. The middle sections explain how the tool works, including search filters, saved searches and personalized plans, and how families can get one-on-one help from local Child Care Resource & Referral Agencies. Next it describes what those agencies are and the free and paid tiers of referral services, including a search widget that employers can add to their own websites. A preview section then walks through the main features with screen-style slides covering search, resource libraries, and parent account tools. The deck closes with a summary of benefits and a contact slide for the digital project manager. Slides worth studying include the problem-and-solution opening on slides 2 and 3, the step-by-step explanation on slide 5, the tier comparison on slides 8 through 10, and the feature preview on slides 12 through 14, which shows the product through simple labeled visuals rather than dense text.
